title: Why Websites Check Your Exact Battery Percentage

vo.en: Check your battery percentage right now.

visual.description: Macro close-up of a man's finger interacting with a glowing battery icon on a smartphone screen in a dark room.

vo.en: Most websites aren't just looking at cookies. They're quietly querying a hidden tool called the Battery Status API.

visual.description: Rapidly scrolling green lines of computer code on a high-tech monitor in a dark office.

vo.en: This reads your exact charge level and discharge rate down to eight decimal places, creating a unique digital signal.

visual.description: A digital display showing rapidly changing decimal numbers and fluctuating bar graphs.

vo.en: But here is the creepy part: going incognito or using a VPN will not stop this tracking.

visual.description: A man wearing a hoodie sitting in front of three glowing monitors, his face partially obscured by shadows.

vo.en: Data brokers use these hyper-specific readings to help fingerprint your device across totally different browsers without your permission.

visual.description: Close up of blue network cables plugged into a blinking server rack in a massive data center.

vo.en: By matching these micro-patterns, they link your private browsing sessions directly back to your real identity.

visual.description: Abstract visualization of glowing dots connecting together to form a digital silhouette of a man.
